== Overview ==
The date of establishment is unknown. According to shrine tradition, during the reign of Emperor Sujin, Ikatakeo-no-Mikoto, a sixth-generation descendant of {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|simple|Nigihayahi|zh|饒速日命|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}, dedicated the shrine name “Taki-no-Miya” and became the first saigū (chief ritual officiant) (according to the shrine notice board).

The shrine buildings stand beside the Taki River, a tributary of the Tonda River, and more than 30 kofun (ancient burial mounds) are clustered in the surrounding area (the prefecturally designated historic site “Taki Shrine Kofun Group”). Near the summit upstream along the Taki River is a sacred rock called Kawakami no Iwao, regarded as the inner sanctuary; it is a {{ill|Iwakura rock|fa|ایواکورا|ja|磐座|ko|이와쿠라|ru|Ивакура (синто)|simple|Iwakura|qid=Q11587880}}. It is said to have divine efficacy for rainmaking, and the shrine is thought to have originated in worship centered on this sacred rock.

The earliest documentary reference appears in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai it was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}.

During the Edo period, it served as a prayer shrine of the Imabari Domain, where rainmaking prayers were performed. At the time of such prayers, the domain lord would worship at the shrine; the first half of the seven-day prayer period was conducted at the main hall, and the latter half at Kawakami no Iwao.
